back: Imports are goods and services bought from other countries; exports are goods and services sold to other countries.
Balance of trade = value of exports − value of imports (of goods). A negative result is a deficit.
Tariffs (tax on imports), quotas (quantity limits), embargoes (bans), standards and licences, and exchange controls.
Raise prices or cut margins, change suppliers or products, produce locally or in a joint venture, or lobby the government.
Preferential trade area, free trade area, customs union, common market, economic union.
Bigger markets without tariffs, cheaper inputs, economies of scale, free movement of capital and sometimes labour.
More competition from partner firms, loss of protection, border delays and unequal gains.
SADC (Southern African Development Community), COMESA (Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa), ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States).
